home.title: A small shop that keeps growing

shop.title: The growing food shop
stage.one-person.title: One person
stage.one-person.summary: You cook, serve and take the money, all by yourself.
stage.order-window.title: The order window
stage.order-window.summary: Customers order at one window, and the kitchen works behind it.
stage.more-hands.title: More hands
stage.more-hands.summary: You hire helpers so more orders can be made at the same time.
stage.long-line.title: The long line
stage.long-line.summary: Three counters are open, but the line is uneven. Who should serve the next customer?
stage.prep-shelf.title: The prep shelf
stage.prep-shelf.summary: Popular items are made ahead and kept within reach.
stage.order-rail.title: The order rail

stage.second-branch.title: A second branch

lesson.title: The long line
lesson.story.heading: The story
lesson.story.p1: The shop got popular. You opened three counters so more people could be served at once.
lesson.story.p2: But the counters are not the same. One worker is very fast. One is new and still learning. And the customers differ too: some buy a single drink, while others order twenty lunch boxes.
lesson.story.p3: At first you send customers to the counters one by one, in turn. It sounds fair, yet it keeps going wrong. The new worker gets stuck on a huge order while the fast worker stands idle, and the line grows.
lesson.story.p4: Taking turns does not keep the work even. Someone has to look at the counters and decide where each customer should go.
lesson.game.heading: Game area
lesson.game.note: The game will be here soon. For now, this is a picture of the three counters.
lesson.term.heading: The engineering term
lesson.term.intro: In software, the same idea has names.
lesson.term.lb.name: Load Balancer
lesson.term.lb.desc: The person who directs customers to the counters is a Load Balancer. It decides where each piece of work goes so that no one is overloaded.
lesson.term.server.name: Server
lesson.term.server.desc: A counter is a server. It is a machine that does the work.
lesson.term.request.name: Request
lesson.term.request.desc: A customer is a request. It is one piece of work that arrives and needs an answer.
